# Oriole of EVV (`oriole-of-evv`)

Checks Medicaid home care claims against electronic visit verification: claim lines with no EVV visit, units above the verified time, visits billed under a different caregiver, visits verified away from the client's address, and caregivers whose share of hand-entered or edited visits is above your limit. Client and caregiver names are masked before results reach the model.

**Oriole never submits or changes claims. Oriole never edits or creates EVV visits.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Home care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y oriole-of-evv demo
npx -y oriole-of-evv mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up home care agency, clients and caregivers. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`evv-visits.csv`](fixtures/evv-visits.csv) and [`claims.csv`](fixtures/claims.csv) for November 2 to 5, 2026. Planted:
  - Abby Lund: November 3 billed 8 units for a 90-minute verified visit (6 units).
  - Bruno Sato: November 4 billed with no EVV visit.
  - Celia Ward: billed under Omar Feld but verified by Tom Baptiste.
  - Dane Ivers: the visit was verified away from the client's address.
  - Lia Gruber: 2 of 3 visits entered or edited by hand, above the 20% limit.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): 15-minute units, midpoint rounding, a 20% manual-edit limit. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `oriole_check` | List claim lines with no visit, units over verified time, caregiver and location mismatches, and caregivers with many manual edits. | runs |
| `oriole_write_report` | Write oriole-evv.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and oriole-evv.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/oriole). | runs |
| `oriole_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `oriole_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `oriole_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `oriole_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `claim_submit` | Oriole never submits or changes claims. | refused |
| `evv_visit_edit` | Oriole never edits or creates EVV visits. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `oriole_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `visits` (required) | EVV visit export under --root: client, caregiver, date, clock in and out (or minutes), service, location verified or distance, manual edit |
| `claims` (required) | Claim lines: client, date of service, service code, units, caregiver, amount |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: unit_minutes, rounding, max_distance, max_manual_pct, min_visits |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx oriole-of-evv inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### EVV visits (`visits`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | text (masked) | Client ID, Client #, Member ID, Medicaid ID, Recipient ID, Participant ID, Patient ID |
| `client_name` | text (masked) | Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Recipient, Participant, Patient Name |
| `caregiver_id` | text (masked) | Caregiver ID, Worker ID, Aide ID, Employee ID, Staff ID, Attendant ID |
| `caregiver_name` | text (masked) | Caregiver, Caregiver Name, Worker, Aide, Employee, Attendant, Staff Name |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `clock_in` | text | Clock In, Check In, Time In, Start, Visit Start |
| `clock_out` | text | Clock Out, Check Out, Time Out, End, Visit End |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `service` | text | Service, Service Code, Procedure, HCPCS, Code, Billing Code |
| `location_ok` | text | Location Verified, GPS Match, Location OK, Location Match, Geo Verified |
| `distance` | number | Distance, Distance from Address, GPS Distance, Miles from Home |
| `manual` | text | Manual, Manual Edit, Edited, Exception, Visit Edited, Adjusted |

### Claims (`claims`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | text (masked) | Client ID, Client #, Member ID, Medicaid ID, Recipient ID, Participant ID, Patient ID |
| `client_name` | text (masked) | Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Recipient, Participant, Patient Name |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `service` | text | Service, Service Code, Procedure, HCPCS, Code, Billing Code |
| `units` | number | Units, Unit, Qty, Quantity, Days/Units, Service Units |
| `caregiver_id` | text (masked) | Caregiver ID, Worker ID, Aide ID, Employee ID, Staff ID, Attendant ID |
| `caregiver_name` | text (masked) | Caregiver, Caregiver Name, Worker, Aide, Employee, Attendant, Staff Name |
| `amount` | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |

## Settings file (`oriole_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `unit_minutes` | Minutes in one billing unit; default 15 |
| `rounding` | How partial units count under your state rules; default midpoint (8 of 15 minutes) |
| `max_distance` | Distance from the client's address above which a visit is flagged, in the unit your EVV export uses |
| `max_manual_pct` | Share of a caregiver's visits entered or edited by hand above which to flag; default 10 |
| `min_visits` | Visits a caregiver needs before the manual-edit share is judged; default 3 |

## Memory

`oriole_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `oriole_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "oriole-of-evv": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "oriole-of-evv",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add oriole-of-evv -- npx -y oriole-of-evv mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
oriole-of-evv tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
oriole-of-evv sources               # the columns each input is read from
oriole-of-evv inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
oriole-of-evv call oriole_check '{"visits":"<visits>","claims":"<claims>"}'
oriole-of-evv eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
oriole-of-evv demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
